Warning the class activities require you to speak in front of the class. He spins a wheel with names and it can be very anxiety inducing. You only have three speeches. Dr. Dunning was a fun professor! His lectures were engaging and he was a lenient grader for our speeches. We would have to read the textbook and he would quiz us on the readings the next class, but they were all very basic and completely understandable. We would also have class activities once a week which was always fun, interactive, and social.

Dr. Dunning is a really chill professor. He's laid back, a little funny, and seemed to adapt well to online learning. There isn't much work in the class, but you do have to read the textbook, or at least skim it, as there are pop quizzes based on the reading. If you have to take an FSOC class(which you do), I wouldn't tell anyone not to take him.

Professor Zafft should stick to teaching the lower level courses. It was disappointing how she offers little to no assistance in a upper sequence required course. It was even more discouraging when a student would inquire about feedback or clarity in an assignment her responses were short as if you are supposed to already know the material.

Rather odd since in academia crediting authors and books are required. It is also a copyright infringement.

Material itself isnt difficult to understand, but the quizzes and exams are more difficult than they should be. The quizzes are short answer instead of MC which makes it harder, and some of the wording for exams could be misinterpreted/tricky. review_highlights.comment: Robyn's been at UMD for 100 years, and doesn't BS her students. It's nice to focus on actually learning rather than stressing over grades - and she knows it. You'll HAVE to read for exams, & she doesn't use ELMS... but super low stress.

Class was pretty good. Shes Sorta old fashioned (doesnt post grades or lectures, uses an attendance book) but nothing wrong with that. We had one personal assignment and a group project. We had two 100 question exams so STUDY, READ AND TAKE NOTES. She always looked for our opinion on stuff. HowverShe could have been clearer on the group prject tho.

My class was basically just conversations about different facets of homophobia in society. It took me a little while to feel comfortable sharing (because I'm not a member of LGBTQI comm. but everyone else was), but once I did, it felt just like a really woke conversation. She cares about the cause and wants everyone to get something out of class.

I took Dr. Zeiger's class for an elective in my major. She is simply just an awesome professor. I would take her again and I will recommend this class to anyone in my major needing an elective. She shares personal stories that relate to lectures when necessary, allowing students to get a better understanding. Come to class, and take notes.

One downside is that her TAs grade papers and they can be a bit harsh at times.

Dr. Zou was one of if not my most favorite professors to have learned from in my college career. She has a level of insight and care when addressing systemic racist issues that's motivated me to want to learn more even outside of the classroom. She focuses her assignments to be more written so you can reflect and personally apply them.

Professor Zou is my favorite professor I've had so far at UMD! I took her PSYC 232 (Psychology of Racism) class first semester, and then PSYC 221 second semester. She is relatable, caring, and gives extremely interesting lectures. She is very accommodating to your needs and overall is an amazing professor. Take her classes if you can!

She is a great teacher and her lectures were very easy to follow. There are a few essays you have to write but the rubric is clear and the TAs are very useful for answering questions.
